headline: High: open-webui can feed prompts/files into Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP/OpenAPI tools and browser/file inputs, so attacker-controlled content can enter its prompts. Perplexity performs vendor-hosted multi-hop browsing and returns cited answers, so if open-webui forwards those outputs into downstream prompting, instruction hijack is plausible. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards Perplexity outputs into a prompt without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF either side ingests web page text or uploaded documents as instructions, attacker content can steer the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt chaining from Perplexity into open-webui.
Strip or quote retrieved text before reuse in prompts.
Use a fixed system prompt that forbids following retrieved instructions.
Review one representative workflow for raw HTML/text ingestion.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to retrieved snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, documents, notes, calendar events, persistent memory, and API keys, while Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor APIs. If open-webui passes sensitive local content into Perplexity, data can leave the host to a third party by default. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so uncertainty is handled conservatively at high severity.
conditions: IF open-webui sends local files, notes, or API-key-bearing context to Perplexity, those data leave the host.
IF Perplexity is used on uploaded PDFs or images containing secrets, vendor-side retention/exposure applies.
mitigations: Block secrets and API keys from any Perplexity-bound prompt.
Use a redaction step before upload or query forwarding.
Restrict open-webui connectors to non-sensitive workspaces.
Turn off automatic file attachment to search queries.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP rules on outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write local files and mounted volumes, while Perplexity cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or execute shell. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is browser-based interaction and shared user context, so the blast radius is limited and no strong contention primitive is documented.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same mutable directory through open-webui mounts, local file contention can occur.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to one shared resource, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent.
Keep Perplexity read-only in shared workflows.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same file set.
Use manual handoff instead of simultaneous writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act as an orchestrator over tools and persistent memory, and Perplexity is a citation-producing search agent. If open-webui treats Perplexity’s answers as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream prompts or actions. Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing is helpful but not a verification boundary, so the interaction exists in common default usage patterns.
conditions: IF open-webui reuses Perplexity answers without a verification step, hallucinations can propagate.
IF open-webui triggers follow-on actions from cited answers, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on Perplexity output.
Ask open-webui to cross-check critical claims with a second source.
Mark Perplexity answers as untrusted in prompts.
Limit automation to read-only summarization.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, and local files, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible residency/retention mismatch for sensitive data classes, especially if regulated content is forwarded from open-webui into Perplexity. The profiles do not document a DPA or residency guarantee, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are forwarded from open-webui to Perplexity, residency/retention review is required.
IF API keys or persistent memory are included in uploaded documents, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Perplexity prompts.
Confirm retention and deletion settings for both services.
Route sensitive workloads to a compliant local-only path.
Document a data-class allowlist for cross-agent use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
